summary: Defines a profile of TLS 1.2 that is fully compliant with the US government's NSA Suite B cryptography policy. It obsoletes RFC 5430. It is informational, its status is now historic, and RFC 8996 later updated it.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines a TLS profile that restricts negotiation to algorithms in the NSA Suite B cryptography policy. It specifies requirements for cipher suites, curves, signatures, and certificates.

questions: what cipher suites does suite b tls use
which curves does suite b allow
subtitle: A profile that limits TLS 1.2 to cryptographic algorithms in the NSA Suite B policy.

tldr.problem: Suite B policy specifies algorithms for national security applications, while TLS can negotiate among many algorithms and curves.
tldr.mechanism: The profile selects TLS 1.2 cipher suites using AES-GCM, ECDH, and ECDSA with specified curves and hashes for two minimum security levels.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6460 is Historic. It obsoletes RFC 5430 and is updated by RFC 8996 according to the unit metadata.

today: RFC 6460 is Historic. It obsoletes RFC 5430 and is listed as updated by RFC 8996.

sections.title: A Suite B Profile for TLS
sections.content:
The RFC defines a profile for using NSA Suite B Cryptography with TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2. It does not create new cipher suites; it selects from suites defined by other specifications.

RFC 6460 obsoletes RFC 5430. It moves the earlier transitional profile for TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, and DTLS 1.0 to an annex, where it is described as transitional rather than Suite B compliant.
sections.plainLanguage: This profile narrows the TLS choices to algorithms allowed by Suite B. The RFC also keeps an older transitional profile in an annex.

sections.title: The Two Minimum Security Levels
sections.content:
Suite B defines minimum security levels of 128 bits and 192 bits. The 128-bit level allows either of two complete combinations: AES with a 128-bit key in GCM mode and P-256, or AES with a 256-bit key in GCM mode and P-384. Each combination also specifies the corresponding TLS pseudorandom function hash.

The 192-bit level requires the combination using AES-256, P-384, and SHA-384. Suite B peers may be configured to accept non-Suite B suites for compatibility, but two Suite B systems establishing a TLS 1.2 session must use Suite B algorithms.
sections.plainLanguage: The lower security level permits two algorithm combinations. The 192-bit level permits only the combination using the larger AES key and P-384.

sections.title: Cipher Suites and Curve Selection
sections.content:
Suite B TLS requires TLS 1.2 or later because the profile uses GCM cipher suites. A 128-bit client offers the AES-128-GCM suite before the AES-256-GCM suite. A 192-bit client offers the AES-256-GCM suite and must not offer the AES-128-GCM suite.

Connections use secp256r1 or secp384r1, with the curve paired to the selected AES key size. The server must not select a non-Suite B curve. If the client offers no acceptable curve, the server ends the handshake with a fatal handshake_failure alert.
sections.plainLanguage: The client and server choose from a limited set of cipher suites and curves. The server ends the handshake if the client offers no allowed curve.

sections.title: ECDSA Authentication and Certificates
sections.content:
Suite B TLS uses ECDSA for authentication. At the 128-bit level, a party may use ECDSA-256 or ECDSA-384; at the 192-bit level, it must use ECDSA-384. The client must authenticate the server, while the server may authenticate the client.

Certificates used for a Suite B TLS connection must be signed with ECDSA and follow the Suite B certificate profile. The client and server also advertise and use the supported ECDSA and hash algorithms during the handshake.
sections.plainLanguage: Both parties use ECDSA signatures with the allowed curves and hashes. The client must verify the server, and the certificate must follow the Suite B profile.

sections.title: The Older Transitional Profile
sections.content:
The annex describes a profile for TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, and DTLS 1.0. It uses Suite B algorithms as far as those protocol versions allow, including AES in CBC mode, ECDH on P-256 or P-384, and HMAC with SHA-1.

The RFC explicitly says this transitional profile is not Suite B compliant. It is described as a path toward the profile for newer TLS versions.
sections.plainLanguage: The annex gives older TLS versions a transitional set of choices. The RFC says that profile does not meet full Suite B compliance.
